paper_metadata.title: Quantum Optimization for Portfolio Management in Financial Services Using the Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) Algorithm

summary: The paper studies VQE for 20-stock portfolio optimization and reports risk variance of 0.0147, expected return of 9.32%, and Sharpe ratio of 0.624. Classical baselines MVO and Black-Litterman are faster to converge (15 s and 25 s versus 120 s), so the paper shows better portfolio quality metrics for VQE but not a runtime advantage.

experiments.description: VQE-based portfolio optimization on a 20-stock sample, compared against classical mean-variance optimization and Black-Litterman model; evaluated on risk, expected return, Sharpe ratio, and convergence time.

algorithm.variant: standard hybrid VQE for portfolio optimization

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Portfolio weights are represented in the quantum circuit; the paper does not specify a binary/QUBO encoding or qubit-to-variable mapping.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize portfolio risk (variance) and maximize expected return, expressed as H(w) = alpha * w^T Σ w - beta * w^T r (paper gives this in descriptive form, with notation partially garbled in the text).
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H(w) representing portfolio risk/return tradeoff; described as a Hamiltonian for VQE optimization.

problem_instance.description: Portfolio selection/asset allocation for financial services using a sample of 20 stocks.
problem_instance.dataset_name: Yahoo Finance / Quandl / Bloomberg (sources mentioned generically)

dataset_specification.description: Historical stock prices for 20 liquid shares; paper mentions 5-10 years of daily closing prices as intended data preparation, but the exact realized date range and tickers are not reported.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Compute expected returns, variance/covariance matrix, volatility, and possibly Value at Risk from historical daily closing prices; include transaction cost, liquidity, and risk tolerance considerations.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Comparison against classical MVO and Black-Litterman using portfolio risk (variance), expected return, Sharpe ratio, and convergence time; results reported for the 20-asset sample.

implementation_details.classical_solver: Classical mean-variance optimization and Black-Litterman model used as baselines; classical optimizer for VQE not specified.
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Historical price data used to compute returns, covariance matrix, volatility, and related portfolio statistics.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute and compare risk, expected return, Sharpe ratio, and convergence time across VQE, MVO, and BLM.

speedup_claims.conditions: 20-asset portfolio optimization on the reported implementation
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports better portfolio quality metrics for VQE but longer convergence time than classical baselines; no asymptotic or empirical speedup is demonstrated.

complexity_analysis.wall_clock_classical: 15 s for MVO; 25 s for BLM

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not enough information to estimate; paper reports use of IBM Quantum Experience/Qiskit but no qubit count, circuit depth, or device details.

speedup_order set to none_proven because the paper reports better portfolio metrics but longer convergence time than classical baselines and does not establish asymptotic quantum speedup.

The paper reports VQE has lower variance (0.0147 vs 0.0152 and 0.0155), higher expected return (9.32% vs 8.85% and 8.9%), and higher Sharpe ratio (0.624 vs 0.593 and 0.608), but longer convergence time (120 s vs 15 s and 25 s).
No asymptotic or practical quantum speedup is demonstrated.
